Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 87, verse 1:

Indeed all praise is due to Allah. We praise Him, seek His help and ask His forgiveness, and we seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and the bad consequences of our deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can misguide; and whomever He leaves to stray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. May Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, his family, his companions, and all who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgement.

To proceed: we begin this, our second weekly session of the month of Rajab in the year one thousand four hundred and fourteen (after the Hijra), which takes place every Thursday, by commenting on Surah (Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High). This is because our course of commentary on Juz' 'Amma (Juz' an-Naba') has reached this surah, and we chose to explain the short surahs of the mufassal, since they are recited often in the prayers by the general public.

The Qur'an was revealed for three matters:

The first: worship of Allah, the Exalted, through its recitation, which carries reward, for whoever recites a letter of the Qur'an will have ten good deeds for it.

The second: reflection upon its meanings.

The third: taking admonition from it. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿A Book which We have revealed to you, blessed, that they may reflect upon its verses and that people of understanding may take heed﴾ [Sad 29].

No one can be reminded by the Qur'an unless he knows its meaning, because one who does not know its meaning is in the position of one who does not read, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones who know not the Book except wishful thinking﴾ [Al-Baqarah 78], meaning: except recitation. Therefore it is incumbent upon the Muslim to strive to know the meaning of the Qur'an so that he benefits from it, and so that he follows the footsteps of the early generations (al-Salaf); for they would not move on from ten verses until they had learned them and what they contain of knowledge and action. So we begin with the first surah: (Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High).

The basmalah has already been discussed, and that it is an independent verse of the Book of Allah, not part of al-Fatihah, nor of al-Baqarah, nor of Al 'Imran, nor of any surah of the Qur'an; rather it is an independent verse revealed at the beginning of every surah. For this reason, the correct view is that the first verse of al-Fatihah is: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾; the second: ﴿The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾; the third: ﴿Sovereign of the Day of Recompense﴾; the fourth: ﴿It is You we worship and You we ask for help﴾; the fifth: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾; the sixth: ﴿The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour﴾; and the seventh: ﴿not of those who have evoked anger or of those who are astray﴾. This is the correct view, which is indicated by the Sunnah of the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family.

Allah says: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [Al-A'la 1]. The address here is to the Messenger, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, and the address directed to the Messenger in the Noble Qur'an is of three types:

The first type: that evidence establishes it is specific to him, so it is specific to him.

The second: that evidence establishes it is general, so it is general.

The third: that no evidence indicates either this or that, so it is specific to him in wording, but general to him and to the Ummah in ruling.

An example of the first is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast? And We removed from you your burden﴾ [Al-Sharh 1-2]. Another example is His saying: ﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a Messenger﴾ [An-Nisa' 79]; it is well known that this is specific to the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family.

An example of the second, where the address to the Messenger, peace be upon him, contains an indication of generality, is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their waiting period﴾ [At-Talaq 1]. He first addressed the Messenger, peace be upon him, saying: ﴿O Prophet﴾, and did not say: "O you who have believed, when you divorce"; He said: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce﴾, and did not say: "O Prophet, when you (singular) divorce." He said: ﴿O Prophet, when you (plural) divorce﴾. This indicates that the address directed to the Messenger, peace be upon him, is directed to him and to the Ummah.

As for examples of the third type, they are very numerous: Allah addresses the Messenger, peace be upon him, while what is meant is the address to him in wording and generality in ruling.

Here Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾. ﴿Glorify﴾ means: declare Allah free of everything that does not befit His majesty and greatness, for tasbih means tanzih (declaring transcendence). When you say "Subhan Allah," it means that I declare Allah free of every evil, every defect, every deficiency. For this reason, among the names of Allah are al-Salam and al-Quddus, because He is exempt from every defect. We will give you examples:

Among the attributes of Allah is life (al-Hayah). Is there any deficiency in His life? No. The life of a created being has deficiency: first, because it is preceded by non-existence, since man is not eternal; and second, because it is followed by annihilation: ﴿Everyone upon it will perish﴾ [Ar-Rahman 26].

Hearing (al-Sam'): does the hearing of Allah, mighty and majestic, have any deficiency? The answer: No, it has no deficiency. He hears everything. Even the woman who came complaining to the Prophet ﷺ, whose story Allah mentioned in Surah al-Mujadilah, was speaking to the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, while 'Aishah was in the room and some of her speech was hidden from her, and Allah said in His Book: ﴿Allah has heard the speech of the one who argues with you concerning her husband﴾ [Al-Mujadilah 1]. For this reason 'Aishah said: "Praise be to Allah, whose hearing encompasses all voices. Indeed the woman who argued was complaining to the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, and some of her speech was hidden from me."[[Recorded by al-Nasa'i (3460) and Ibn Majah (188) from 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "Praise be to Allah whose hearing encompasses all voices. Khawlah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ complaining about her husband, and some of her words were hidden from me, so Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Allah has heard the speech of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual exchange﴾ [Al-Mujadilah 1] and the rest of the verse."]] So the meaning of ﴿Glorify﴾ (Subhan Allah) is: what? I declare Allah free of every defect and deficiency.

As for His saying: ﴿the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾, some exegetes said that His saying ﴿the name of your Lord﴾ means the named one, your Lord, because glorification is not for the name itself but for Allah Himself. However, the correct view is that its meaning is: glorify your Lord while mentioning His name; that is, do not glorify Him with the heart only, but glorify Him with the heart and the tongue, by mentioning His name, the Exalted. This meaning is supported by His saying: ﴿So glorify with the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah 74], meaning: glorify with glorification joined to the name. This is because glorifying Allah may be by the heart, through belief, and may be by the tongue, and may be by both together; and the intended meaning is that one glorifies with both together: with the heart, uttering with the tongue.

As for His saying: ﴿your Lord﴾, al-Rabb means: the Creator, the Owner, the Manager of all affairs. Allah is the Creator, the Owner, and the Manager of all affairs.

Do the polytheists acknowledge this?

The answer: Yes, they acknowledge it: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [Luqman 25], and ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created them?" they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 87]. Allah, glorified and exalted, informed that when they are asked: ﴿Who controls hearing and sight, and who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living, and who arranges the matter?—they will say, "Allah"﴾ [Yunus 31]. Thus they acknowledge that Allah possesses dominion, has the power of disposal, and is the Creator. But they worship others alongside Him out of ignorance. How can you acknowledge that Allah alone is the Creator, Owner, and Manager of all affairs, and yet worship others with Him?! So the meaning of Rabb according to this is: the Creator, Owner, and Manager of all affairs. Every person who acknowledges this is obliged not to worship except Allah, as the many verses indicate: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you﴾ [Al-Baqarah 21]. He said: ﴿worship your Lord who created you﴾, meaning: do not worship other than Him.

﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾. ﴿The Most High﴾ derives from highness (al-'uluw), and Allah's highness, mighty and majestic, is of two kinds: highness of attributes and highness of essence.

As for the highness of attributes, the most perfect attributes belong to Allah, mighty and majestic; He said: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest description﴾ [An-Nahl 60].

As for the highness of essence, it is that Allah, the Exalted, is above His servants, established upon His Throne. When a person says, "O Allah," where does he direct himself?

* Student: To the sky.

* The Shaykh: He directs himself to the sky, upward. Allah, majestic and exalted, is above everything, established upon His Throne.

So, when you recite ﴿the Most High﴾, sense within yourself that Allah is exalted in His attributes and exalted in His essence. For this reason, when a person prostrates he says what? "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High," remembering through his own lowering; because he is now lowered, and this is the lowest that he is. Yet the most noble and highest part of a person is his face, and nevertheless he lowers it, placing it on the earth that is trodden by feet. So it is from wisdom that he says, "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High," meaning: I declare my Lord, who is above everything, free of defect, since I have lowered myself below everything. Thus you glorify Allah the Most High in His attributes and the Most High in His essence, and when you say "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High," you feel that your Lord, exalted, is above everything, and that He is the most perfect of everything in His attributes.

Then He said: ﴿Who created and proportioned﴾ [Al-A'la 2]. "Created" (khalaqa) means: brought into existence from non-existence. Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, is the One who brought into being all created things. Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, said: ﴿O mankind, a parable is presented, so listen to it﴾ [Al-Hajj 73]. Glory be to Allah! Allah says: ﴿O mankind, a parable is presented, so listen,﴾ listen, ﴿Indeed, those you invoke other than Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for that. And if the fly should steal from them a thing, they could not recover it from him﴾ [Al-Hajj 73]. By Allah, it is a great parable. All those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it. Even if all the deities worshipped besides Allah, all the sultans, all the presidents, and all the engineers gathered together to create one fly, they would not be able to do so. Now, in this age, when industry has advanced to this tremendous degree, even if all these creatures gathered together to create a fly, they would not be able to. Even if, as they claim, they have made a mechanical human, they cannot create a fly. This mechanical human is nothing but machinery that moves only, yet it does not get hungry, does not get thirsty, does not feel heat, does not feel cold, and does not move except when moved. No one other than Allah can create a fly. Allah, glorified and exalted, alone is the Creator. And with what does He create? With a single word: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before Allah is like that of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was﴾ [Ali 'Imran 59]. ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin 82]. One word. All creatures die and perish; the earth consumes them, beasts consume them, fires burn them. And when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will call them with a single cry: "Come out!" And they come out. ﴿It will be but one shout, and at once they will be on the surface of the earth﴾ [An-Nazi'at 13, 14]. ﴿It will not be but one shout, and then they will all be brought before Us⁠—present﴾ [Ya-Sin 53]. The entire world of humans, jinn, beasts, insects, and others will all be gathered on the Day of Resurrection with a single word.

So Allah, may He be exalted, alone is the Creator, and none creates with Him. Creation does not burden Him or overpower Him; it is easy for Him, and it happens with a single word.

As for His saying ﴿and proportioned﴾: "He created and proportioned" means: He fashioned what He created in the best form and in the appropriate shape. For example, Allah the Exalted said in Surah Al-Infitar: ﴿Who created you and proportioned you and made you balanced? In whatever form He willed, He assembled you﴾ [Al-Infitar 7, 8]. ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾ [At-Tin 4]. There is nothing among creatures more excellent than the form of man: his head is on top, his heart is in the chest, and he is in a complete state. For this reason, the first thing included in His saying ﴿and proportioned﴾ is the proportioning of man. In ﴿Who created and proportioned﴾, everything is proportioned in the manner that suits it.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 87, verse 3:**

﴿Who measured [everything] and then guided [it]﴾ [al-A'la: 3]. He, the Mighty and Majestic, measured everything, as He said: ﴿And He created everything and measured it precisely﴾ [al-Furqan: 2]. He measured it in its state and its outcome, in its essence and its attributes. Everything has a limited measure: the terms (of life) are limited, the conditions are limited, the bodies are limited; everything is measured with a measure, as He said: ﴿And He created everything and measured it precisely﴾.

His saying ﴿and then guided﴾ includes both legislative guidance (al-hidayah al-shar'iyyah) and universal guidance (al-hidayah al-kawniyyah).

Universal guidance means that Allah guided every thing to what it was created for. Pharaoh said to Musa: ﴿He said, "Then who is the Lord of you two, O Musa?" He said, "Our Lord is He who gave each thing its creation and then guided it"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 49-50]. You find that every creature has been guided by Allah, the Exalted, to what it needs. Consider the infant: when it comes out from its mother's womb and wants to nurse, is there anyone who tells it, "Lift your head, suckle from the breast"? No. Even if no one were there to instruct it, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, guides it to this breast so that it sucks from it. And consider the smallest of insects, the ant, for example: where does it place its homes? It places its homes only in a high place on the earth, on a mound, why? Because it fears floods that would enter its homes and ruin them. Also, when rain comes and there is grain food in its burrows or homes, it brings it out when the sun rises to spread it out. Why? So that it does not rot. And before storing it, it eats the ends of the grain, so that it does not sprout and spoil on them. This is a observed and tested matter. Who guided it to this? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, guided it. This is universal guidance: that He guided every creature to what it needs.

As for legislative guidance, which is the most important for the children of Adam, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has also clarified it, even for the disbelievers; that is, He made it clear to them. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat: 17], and we seek refuge with Allah, they preferred disbelief over faith.

Legislative guidance is the purpose of the life of the children of Adam: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56]. Allah informed us of this so that we would turn to Him in all our affairs. When we know that He is the Creator after non-existence, and illness afflicts us, to whom do we turn? Yes, to Allah; turn to Allah. For He who created you and brought you into existence from nothingness is able to restore your body to health. So turn to your Lord and rely upon Him. There is no harm in taking the medicine He has permitted for you, but with the belief that this medicine, for example, is a cause among the causes which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has made. If you are healed by this cause, who healed you? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It is He who made this medicine a cause of your cure, and if He willed, He would have made this medicine a cause of your destruction. So when we know that Allah is the Creator, we turn in all our affairs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. When we know that He is the Guide, we seek guidance by His guidance, by His law, until we reach what our Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, has prepared for us of honor.

We ask Allah, the Exalted, to guide us and you to the straight path, and to settle us and you in the abode of His honor with those whom Allah has blessed: the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous.

Here ends the discussion of these noble verses. I urge you once more to learn the meanings of the verses of the Qur'an. If you wish to truly benefit from it, then you must know its meaning. But from where? From trustworthy scholars, or from the tafsirs of trustworthy scholars, because people have spoken about the words of Allah and investigated its meanings. Some of them have been guided to the straight path, and some have deviated for one reason or another: either due to deficiency in their knowledge or understanding, or due to bad intention, for a person may be deprived of what is correct because of bad intention, and we seek refuge with Allah.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

(...) We first discuss what remains of Surah (Sabbih isma rabbika al-A'la) from His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿We shall make you recite, so you will not forget, except what Allah wills. Indeed, He knows what is apparent and what is hidden﴾ [Al-A'la 6–7], and ﴿We shall ease you toward ease﴾ [Al-A'la 8]. This is a promise from Allah, glorified and exalted be He, to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and to his family, that He will have him recite the Qur'an and that the Messenger will not forget it. He will have him recite it and he will not forget it. The Messenger (ﷺ) used to hasten when Jibril came to deliver the revelation to him, so Allah said to him: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation. So when We have recited it, follow its recitation. Then upon Us is its explanation﴾ [Al-Qiyamah 16–19]. So the Prophet (ﷺ) would listen attentively until Jibril finished reciting the revelation, and then he would recite it. Here He says: ﴿We shall make you recite, so you will not forget, except what Allah wills﴾, meaning: except what Allah wills that you forget, for the matter is in the hand of the Mighty and Majestic; ﴿Allah erases what He wills and establishes﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 39]; ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring forth one better than it or similar to it. Do you not know that Allah is competent over all things? Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that you have no protector or helper other than Allah?﴾ [Al-Baqarah 106–107]. It may be that the Prophet (ﷺ) forgot a verse of the Book of Allah, but he would quickly recall it, (ﷺ).

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, He knows what is apparent﴾, i.e., Allah, exalted is He, knows what is apparent: what a person utters and speaks audibly.

﴿And what is hidden﴾, i.e., what is concealed and not disclosed, for Allah knows it. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him﴾ [Qaf 16]. So He, Mighty and Majestic, knows what is apparent and also knows what is hidden.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

﴿And what is hidden﴾, i.e., what is concealed and not disclosed, for Allah knows it. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him﴾ [Qaf 16]. So He, Mighty and Majestic, knows what is apparent and also knows what is hidden.

﴿And We will ease you toward ease.﴾ This is also a promise from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to His Messenger ﷺ that He will make things easy for him toward ease. So what is "ease"?

"Ease" means that his affairs will be made easy, especially in obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. When the Prophet ﷺ informed us that there is no one among the people except that his seat has been written for him, from Paradise and from the Fire, that every child of Adam has a seat written for him from Paradise if he is among the people of Paradise, and from the Fire if he is among the people of the Fire, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not leave off action and rely (ye'nī on what has been written)?" He said: "No, act, for each is made easy for that for which he was created." So the people of happiness are made easy for the deeds of the people of happiness, and the people of misery are made easy for the deeds of the people of misery. Then he recited the words of the Most High: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best reward, We will ease him toward ease. But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best reward, We will ease him toward hardship.﴾ [al-Layl 5–10][[Narrated by Muslim (2647/6) from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu) with the wording: "Act, for each is made easy; as for the people of happiness, they are made easy for the deeds of the people of happiness, and as for the people of misery, they are made easy for the deeds of the people of misery." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best reward, We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best reward, We will ease him toward hardship.﴾ [al-Layl 5–10].]]

This hadith refutes the argument of one who uses predestination (qadar) as an excuse for disobeying Allah, who disobeys and says: "This was written for me." We say: this is an error, because the Messenger ﷺ said: "Act, for each is made easy for that for which he was created." Does anyone prevent you from righteous action if you wish to do it? Never. Does anyone compel you to sin if you do not want it? Never, no one. Therefore, if someone compelled you to sin and forced you to it, you would bear no sin, and your act would not carry the same consequences as the act of one who chose it. Even disbelief, which is the greatest of sins, Allah the Most High said concerning it: ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief, except one who has been forced while his heart remains firm in faith, but whoever opens his breast to disbelief, upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment.﴾ [an-Naḥl 106]. So we say: act, O human being, do good, avoid evil, so that Allah makes you easy toward ease and keeps you away from hardship. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was promised by Allah that He would make him easy toward ease, and would facilitate his affairs. For this reason, the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, never fell into hardship or distress without finding a way out for him, peace and blessings be upon him.

Then Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to remind, saying: ﴿So remind, if the reminder benefits﴾ [Al-A'la 9]. That is: remind the people; remind them with the signs of Allah, remind them with the days of Allah, admonish them.

﴿If the reminder benefits﴾ means: in a situation where the reminder benefits. On this basis, ﴿if﴾ (in) is conditional, and the meaning is: if the reminder benefits, then remind; and if it does not benefit, then do not remind, because there is no benefit in reminding a people whom we know will not benefit. This is what has been said regarding this verse.

Some scholars said: the meaning is: remind in every case, if these people are ones in whom the reminder benefits. So the condition here is not intended to mean that one reminds only when it benefits; rather the meaning is: remind, if these people are ones in whom reminding benefits. According to this view, the meaning is: remind in every case, and the reminder will benefit. Benefit whom? It benefits the believers, and it benefits the one who reminds as well. The one who reminds benefits in every case, and the one who is reminded, if he benefits from it, then he is a believer; and if he does not benefit from it, that does not diminish the reward of the one who reminds in the least. Therefore we remind, whether the reminder benefits or does not benefit.

Some scholars said: if one thinks that the reminder will benefit, it becomes obligatory; and if one thinks it will not benefit, he has a choice: if he wills he reminds, and if he wills he does not remind. But in every case we say: reminding is necessary, even if you think it will not benefit, for it will benefit you yourself, and the people will know that this matter about which you reminded is either obligatory or forbidden. If you remain silent while the people are committing what is forbidden, the people will say: "If this were forbidden, the scholars would have reminded about it," or: "If this were obligatory, the scholars would have reminded about it." So reminding is necessary, and spreading the Shariah is necessary, whether it benefits or does not benefit.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, mentioned who will be reminded and who will not be reminded, and we will speak about it, if Allah wills, in the next session or the next meeting.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 87, verse 10–13:

(...) The subject of the introduction to this lesson is the discussion of God's words, blessed and exalted, in Surah al-A'la: ﴿So remind, if the reminder should benefit. He who fears [God] will be reminded, and the wretchedest will avoid it﴾ [al-A'la 10, 11], and so on to the end.

Allah, exalted is He, commanded His Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, to remind, saying: ﴿So remind, if the reminder should benefit﴾, then He said: ﴿He who fears [God] will be reminded, and the wretchedest will avoid it﴾. Thus Allah, exalted is He, made clear that after the reminder people divide into two groups:

The first group: those who fear Allah, mighty and majestic; that is, they fear Him with a fear born of knowledge, because of the greatness of the Creator, exalted is He. When such a person is reminded of the signs of his Lord, he takes heed, as God said describing the servants of the Most Merciful: ﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the signs of their Lord, do not fall upon them deaf and blind﴾ [al-Furqan 73]. So whoever fears Allah and is conscious of Allah, when he is reminded and admonished with the signs of Allah, he takes heed and benefits.

As for the second group, He said: ﴿and the wretchedest will avoid it﴾, that is, the wretchedest avoids this reminder and does not benefit from it.

To proceed: this is the fifty-third session of the series called the "Open Door" sessions, and it is the fourth session in the month of Shawwal in the year 1414 AH. We will speak briefly on what remains of Surah al-A'la, namely the words of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾ [al-A'la 14–15].

﴿Aflaha﴾ (has succeeded) is derived from al-falah (success). Al-falah is a comprehensive word. It means attaining what is sought and being saved from what is feared. This is the meaning of falah: it is a word that includes every good and repels every evil.

His words ﴿man tazakka﴾ (whoever purifies himself) are derived from tazkiyah, which means purification. From it zakah (almsgiving) takes its name, because it purifies the person from the morals of vice, the morals of stinginess, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them﴾ [al-Tawbah 103]. So ﴿tazakka﴾ means "purified himself."

From what does one purify oneself?

First, one purifies oneself from shirk in regard to one's dealings with Allah. He worships Allah, sincere to Him in religion, not showing off and not seeking to be heard, and seeks no status or leadership in what he worships Allah with. Rather, he intends by it the face of Allah and the Hereafter.

He purifies himself in following the Messenger (peace be upon him), such that he does not innovate (bid'ah) in his sharia, neither a little nor a lot, neither in belief, nor in statements, nor in actions.

This, meaning purification with regard to the Messenger (peace be upon him), which is following without innovating, applies fully only to the Salafi method, the way of the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah), who believe in everything Allah described Himself with in His Book or upon the tongue of His Messenger (may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family). It is the Salafi method, whose adherents do not innovate anything in God's religion in verbal acts of worship or in physical acts of worship. You find them following what the sharia has brought, unlike what some innovators do with invented adhkar (remembrances), whether in their type, their manner, their description, or their performance, as some of the Sufi orders and others do.

Likewise, he purifies himself in his dealings with creation, such that he purifies his heart from ghill (rancor) and hatred toward his Muslim brothers. You will find him always pure of heart, loving for his brothers what he loves for himself, not wishing that harm touch anyone, but rather wishing that all people be safe from every evil and granted success in every good.

So purification has three objects: the first concerns the right of Allah, the second concerns the right of the Messenger, and the third concerns the general people.

Regarding the right of Allah: he purifies himself from shirk, so he worships Allah the Exalted, sincere to Him in religion.

Regarding the right of the Messenger: he purifies himself from innovation, so he worships Allah according to the requirements of the Prophet's sharia (peace be upon him) in belief, speech and action.

In dealing with people: he purifies himself from rancor, hatred, enmity and hostility, and everything that brings these about. He avoids everything that brings enmity and hostility among the Muslims, and does everything that brings affection and love. Among this is spreading the greeting of peace, about which the Messenger (peace be upon him) said: "By Allah, you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not inform you of something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the greeting of peace among you."[[Recorded by Muslim (54/93) and Abu Dawud (5193), the wording being his, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not direct you to something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the greeting of peace among you."]]. Greeting with peace is one of the strongest causes of love and affection among the Muslims, and this is something observed: if a man passes by you and does not greet you, something settles in your soul; and if you do not greet him, something settles in his soul. But if you greet him, or he greets you, this becomes like a bond between you that necessitates affection and love. The Prophet (peace be upon him) also said about greeting: "And you greet those you know and those you do not know."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (12) and Muslim (39/63), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (may Allah be pleased with them both).]]

Most people today, when they greet, greet only those they know, and do not greet those they do not know. This is an error, because when you greet only those you know, the greeting is not purely for Allah. Greet those you know and those you do not know among the Muslims, so that you attain the love of the Muslims for one another and the completion of faith, and the ultimate end is entry into Paradise. May Allah make us and you among its people.

His words ﴿wa dhakara isma rabbihi fasalla﴾ (and remembers the name of his Lord and prays) [al-A'la 15] mean: he remembers the name of Allah the Exalted by worshipping Him, and so he prays. Included in remembering the name of Allah is, for example, wudu' (ablution). Wudu' is a remembrance of the name of Allah: first, because a person performs wudu' only in compliance with Allah's command; second, because when he begins his wudu' he says "In the name of Allah," and when he finishes he says: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. O Allah, make me among those who repent and make me among those who purify themselves."

Also among the remembrance of Allah the Mighty and Majestic is the Friday sermon (khutbat al-Jumu'ah), for the Friday sermon is a remembrance of Allah, due to the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 9]. Accordingly, His words ﴿wa dhakara isma rabbihi﴾ mean the preacher on Friday, ﴿fasalla﴾ meaning the Friday prayer. This verse includes every prayer that is preceded by a remembrance, and every prayer is generally preceded by a remembrance. Yes, a person may pray a prayer for which he performed wudu' earlier, but generally a person performs wudu' shortly before the prayer, then remembers the name of Allah, and then prays.

* * *

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the fifty-eighth session of the Open Door series, which we began after the end of the Hajj season, on Thursday the twenty-second of Dhu al-Hijjah in the year 1414 AH. We ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to conclude our year with goodness, pardon and forgiveness.

Remaining for us from the tafsir of Surah al-A'la is the saying of Allah the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿So remind, if the reminder should benefit. He who fears will be reminded, and it will be avoided by the most wretched, who will enter the greatest Fire, in which he will neither die nor live. He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays. But you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring. Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾ [al-A'la 9–19].

Remaining from His words ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself﴾: this sentence is a verbal sentence emphasized with qad (certainly), ﴿qad aflaha﴾. Al-falah is a general word by which is meant escape from what is disliked and attainment of what is loved.

His words ﴿man tazakka﴾ mean: whoever purifies his outward and inward self. His inward self is purified from shirk with Allah the Mighty and Majestic, from doubt, from hypocrisy, from enmity toward the Muslims and hatred, and other things from which the heart must be purified. His outward self is purified from letting his tongue and limbs run loose in aggression against the servants of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. So he does not backbite anyone, does not carry tales about anyone, does not revile anyone, and does not transgress against anyone by beating, denying his property, or otherwise. Thus tazakki is a general word that includes purification from every outward or inward impurity.

﴿wa dhakara isma rabbihi fasalla﴾: ﴿dhakara isma rabbihi﴾ means he remembers Allah. But He, glorified and exalted, mentioned "the name" so that the remembrance would be by the tongue, because remembrance by the tongue involves the tongue pronouncing the name of Allah, such as saying "Glory be to Allah," "Praise be to Allah," or "Allah is greatest," thus remembering the name of Allah.

Some scholars have stated that what is meant here by remembering the name of Allah is the Friday sermon, due to His saying afterward ﴿fasalla﴾. But the correct view is that it is more general than this, and that what is meant is every remembrance of the name of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. That is, whenever a person remembers the name of Allah, he takes admonition, turns toward Allah, and prays. The prayer (salah) is well known: it is an act of worship consisting of statements and actions, opened with takbir (saying Allahu akbar) and closed with taslim (saying the greeting of peace).

Earlier, the discussion of Allah's words ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾ [al-A'la 14–15] was already covered, and we explained that the meaning of ﴿purifies himself﴾ is within himself, that is, he purifies it and removes it from the filth of shirk to the purity of tawhid (monotheism).

We will, God willing, come to the rest of the discussion of the surah later, so as to make room for the brothers.

Likewise, he purifies himself in his dealings with creation, such that he purifies his heart from ghill (rancor) and hatred toward his Muslim brothers. You will find him always pure of heart, loving for his brothers what he loves for himself, not wishing that harm touch anyone, but rather wishing that all people be safe from every evil and granted success in every good.

So purification has three objects: the first concerns the right of Allah, the second concerns the right of the Messenger, and the third concerns the general people.

Regarding the right of Allah: he purifies himself from shirk, so he worships Allah the Exalted, sincere to Him in religion.

Regarding the right of the Messenger: he purifies himself from innovation, so he worships Allah according to the requirements of the Prophet's sharia (peace be upon him) in belief, speech and action.

In dealing with people: he purifies himself from rancor, hatred, enmity and hostility, and everything that brings these about. He avoids everything that brings enmity and hostility among the Muslims, and does everything that brings affection and love. Among this is spreading the greeting of peace, about which the Messenger (peace be upon him) said: "By Allah, you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not inform you of something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the greeting of peace among you."[[Recorded by Muslim (54/93) and Abu Dawud (5193), the wording being his, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not direct you to something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the greeting of peace among you."]]. Greeting with peace is one of the strongest causes of love and affection among the Muslims, and this is something observed: if a man passes by you and does not greet you, something settles in your soul; and if you do not greet him, something settles in his soul. But if you greet him, or he greets you, this becomes like a bond between you that necessitates affection and love. The Prophet (peace be upon him) also said about greeting: "And you greet those you know and those you do not know."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (12) and Muslim (39/63), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (may Allah be pleased with them both).]]

Most people today, when they greet, greet only those they know, and do not greet those they do not know. This is an error, because when you greet only those you know, the greeting is not purely for Allah. Greet those you know and those you do not know among the Muslims, so that you attain the love of the Muslims for one another and the completion of faith, and the ultimate end is entry into Paradise. May Allah make us and you among its people.

His words ﴿wa dhakara isma rabbihi fasalla﴾ (and remembers the name of his Lord and prays) [al-A'la 15] mean: he remembers the name of Allah the Exalted by worshipping Him, and so he prays. Included in remembering the name of Allah is, for example, wudu' (ablution). Wudu' is a remembrance of the name of Allah: first, because a person performs wudu' only in compliance with Allah's command; second, because when he begins his wudu' he says "In the name of Allah," and when he finishes he says: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. O Allah, make me among those who repent and make me among those who purify themselves."

Also among the remembrance of Allah the Mighty and Majestic is the Friday sermon (khutbat al-Jumu'ah), for the Friday sermon is a remembrance of Allah, due to the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 9]. Accordingly, His words ﴿wa dhakara isma rabbihi﴾ mean the preacher on Friday, ﴿fasalla﴾ meaning the Friday prayer. This verse includes every prayer that is preceded by a remembrance, and every prayer is generally preceded by a remembrance. Yes, a person may pray a prayer for which he performed wudu' earlier, but generally a person performs wudu' shortly before the prayer, then remembers the name of Allah, and then prays.

* * *

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the fifty-eighth session of the Open Door series, which we began after the end of the Hajj season, on Thursday the twenty-second of Dhu al-Hijjah in the year 1414 AH. We ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to conclude our year with goodness, pardon and forgiveness.

Remaining for us from the tafsir of Surah al-A'la is the saying of Allah the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿So remind, if the reminder should benefit. He who fears will be reminded, and it will be avoided by the most wretched, who will enter the greatest Fire, in which he will neither die nor live. He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays. But you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring. Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾ [al-A'la 9–19].

Remaining from His words ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself﴾: this sentence is a verbal sentence emphasized with qad (certainly), ﴿qad aflaha﴾. Al-falah is a general word by which is meant escape from what is disliked and attainment of what is loved.

His words ﴿man tazakka﴾ mean: whoever purifies his outward and inward self. His inward self is purified from shirk with Allah the Mighty and Majestic, from doubt, from hypocrisy, from enmity toward the Muslims and hatred, and other things from which the heart must be purified. His outward self is purified from letting his tongue and limbs run loose in aggression against the servants of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. So he does not backbite anyone, does not carry tales about anyone, does not revile anyone, and does not transgress against anyone by beating, denying his property, or otherwise. Thus tazakki is a general word that includes purification from every outward or inward impurity.

﴿wa dhakara isma rabbihi fasalla﴾: ﴿dhakara isma rabbihi﴾ means he remembers Allah. But He, glorified and exalted, mentioned "the name" so that the remembrance would be by the tongue, because remembrance by the tongue involves the tongue pronouncing the name of Allah, such as saying "Glory be to Allah," "Praise be to Allah," or "Allah is greatest," thus remembering the name of Allah.

Some scholars have stated that what is meant here by remembering the name of Allah is the Friday sermon, due to His saying afterward ﴿fasalla﴾. But the correct view is that it is more general than this, and that what is meant is every remembrance of the name of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. That is, whenever a person remembers the name of Allah, he takes admonition, turns toward Allah, and prays. The prayer (salah) is well known: it is an act of worship consisting of statements and actions, opened with takbir (saying Allahu akbar) and closed with taslim (saying the greeting of peace).

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Nay, you prefer the worldly life (16), while the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ [Al-A'la 16–17]. ﴿Nay﴾ (بل) here is for transition (al-idrab al-intiqali). Because "bal" comes for cancellation (al-idrab al-ibtali) and comes for transition (al-idrab al-intiqali); meaning, He, glory be to Him, moved on to explain the state of man, that he prefers the worldly life because it is hasty, and man was created from haste and loves what involves haste. So you find him preferring the worldly life, and in reality it is, by its description, "dunya": "dunya" in time, and "dunya" in description. As for it being "dunya" in time, it is because it precedes the Hereafter, so it is ahead of it, and "al-dhuww" means nearness. As for it being a "dunya" (lowly, deficient) one, that too is the reality, for the worldly life, however long it lasts for a person, its term is extinction; its end is extinction, and however much it flourishes for a person, its outcome is withering. For this reason, hardly does a day pass over you in joy without being followed by sorrow. On this the poet says:

"So one day is for us and one day against us,
and one day we are made to suffer and one day we are made happy."

Reflect on your state in this world and you will find that no time passes for you in which purity is always present; rather, there must be some turbidity. Joy is not always constant; rather, there must be sorrow. Rest is not always constant; rather, there must be fatigue. So the worldly life is "dunya" in accordance with its name.

﴿And the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾. The Hereafter is better than the worldly life and more enduring. Better: in it is bliss and lasting joy that is not spoiled by turbidity; ﴿No fatigue will touch them therein, nor will they be removed from it﴾ [Al-Hijr 48]. Likewise, it is also more enduring than this world, because the survival of this world, as we have previously stated, is brief, transient and fading, unlike the survival of the Hereafter, which is forever and ever.

The commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 87, verses 18–19:

﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾ [al-A'la: 18, 19].

﴿Indeed, this﴾ means: what has been mentioned, namely that man prefers the worldly life over the Hereafter and forgets the Hereafter; and likewise what the verses contain of admonitions. ﴿In the former scriptures﴾ means: those that preceded this nation.

﴿The scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾: these are scriptures brought by Abraham and Moses, upon them be peace, and they contain admonitions by which hearts are softened and conditions are set right.

We ask Allah, exalted is He, to make us and you among those who are given good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and to protect us and you from the punishment of the Fire.
